title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 5: will to save tied to will to teach — God did not teach all
pass_a_gloss: This Divine will concerning the salvation of all men is not to be conceived otherwise than that which is joined concerning the instructing of all men. For they are connected by the Apostle: God wills all to be saved, and to come to the knowledge of the truth. But it is most certain, both from the word of God and from the event itself, that God has not had and does not have a will of instructing all, or of leading all one by one to the knowledge of saving truth: Romans x. 14. How shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? or how shall they preach unless they be sent? But God in past generations suffered all nations to walk in their own ways; Acts xiv. 16. And he granted the knowledge of the truth to the Jewish nation alone. After the coming of Christ the light of truth did not at once shine upon all by the will of God. For a time the Apostles were forbidden to go into the way of the Gentiles, Matthew x. 5. A little later they were also forbidden to preach the word in Asia, Acts xvi. 6. And to come down to our own ages, how many nations detected in the New World do we have, to whom through many ages not even the slightest breath of saving truth has reached? Can it be said that God willed those to come to the knowledge of the truth to whom he was unwilling to send heralds of the truth? See Prosper of Aquitaine, on the Chapters of the Gauls, Response 4 and Sentence 4. If therefore they so understand the Apostle's words that they think God, as far as in him lies, wills to give to all and each of the mortals fallen in Adam, for Christ's sake, the knowledge of saving truth and salvation itself, it is necessary either to acknowledge a manifest error in this opinion of theirs, or a manifest weakness in the Divine will; for he who wills, being able, works.
pass_b_english: This divine will for the salvation of all men must be read with the will joined to it — the will to teach all men. Paul binds them: God wills all to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth (1 Timothy 2:4). Yet it is certain from God's word and from history that he has not willed to teach all, or to lead every person one by one to saving truth. Romans 10:14: how will they call on him in whom they have not believed? how believe without hearing? how hear without a preacher? how preach unless they are sent? In past generations God let the nations walk in their own ways (Acts 14:16) and gave knowledge of the truth to Israel alone. After Christ's coming the light did not at once shine on all by his will: for a time the apostles were barred from the Gentile road (Matthew 10:5), and later forbidden to preach in Asia (Acts 16:6). Come to our own age: how many nations found in the New World have for centuries not felt even a breath of saving truth? Can God be said to have willed them to know the truth when he would not send them heralds of it? See Prosper of Aquitaine on the Gallic chapters (Response 4 and Sentence 4). If they take Paul to mean that God, as far as in him lies, wills to give every fallen child of Adam saving knowledge and salvation itself for Christ's sake, you must either call their reading a clear error or confess weakness in the divine will — for the one who wills, and can, acts.
source_text: Voluntas haec Divina de salute omnium hominum, non aliter concipienda, quam illa quae conjungitur de eruditione omnium hominum. Connectuntur enim ab Apostolo; Deus vult omnes salvos fieri, & ad agnitionem veritatis venire. Est autem certissimum, tum ex verbo Dei, tum ex ipso eventu, Deum non habuisse aut habere voluntatem erudiendi omnes, sive perducendi omnes singulatim ad salutiferae veritatis cognitionem: Rom. x. 14. Quomodo invocabunt eum in quem non crediderint? quomodo autem credent ei de quo non audierint? quomodo audient absque praedicante? aut quomodo praedicabunt si non mittantur? At Deus praeteritis generationibus dimisit omnes gentes suis ipsarum viis incedere; Act. xiv. 16. Ac veritatis agnitionem soli nationi Judaeorum concessit. Post Christi adventum lux veritatis non statim omnibus ex voluntate Dei affulsit. Ad tempus prohibiti sunt Apostoli in viam gentium abire, Matth. x. 5. Aliquanto post vetiti sunt etiam ne praedicarent verbum in Asia, Actor. xvi. 6. Atque ut ad nostra secula descendamus, quot nationes in Novo orbe detectas habemus, ad quas salutiferae veritatis per multa secula ne tenuissima quidem aura pervenit? An dici potest Deus voluisse illos ad agnitionem veritatis venire, ad quos noluit praecones veritatis mittere? Videte Prosperum Aquitanicum, ad Capit. Gall. Respons. 4. & Sent. 4. Si itaque sic intelligunt verba Apostoli, ut sentiant Deum, quantum in se est, velle omnes & singulos mortales in Adamo lapsos propter Christum donare salutiferae veritatis cognitione & ipsa salute, aut in hac illorum sententia manifestum errorem, aut in Divina voluntate manifestam infirmitatem agnoscere est necesse; nam volens potens operatur.
